Optimal.Notes: A 20 fps cap synced to the 40 Hz display gives the smoothest pacing the Deck can manage in this sim; FSR at 960x600 upscaled recovers GPU headroom while keeping terrain readable. Reduce Terrain Level of Detail first if flying over dense cities causes drops below 18 fps.

profiles.Summary: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 is one of the most demanding PC games ever released, and running it on the Steam Deck requires significant compromises — expect 20–35 fps at low settings with FSR upscaling. The game is technically Playable (Verified: Playable), but its massive CPU/GPU requirements mean it will never be a smooth experience on Deck hardware without careful tuning.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's extreme PC requirements (recommended GPU is a GTX 970, well above the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class) and general Deck hardware capabilities. On your first run, check fps over a simple airfield with no live weather — if you cannot hold 20 fps there, drop Terrain Level of Detail to 50 and switch to the Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: At this profile the TDP and GPU clock are capped aggressively to stretch battery life; frame rate will be low but the sim remains navigable. Avoid dense photogrammetry cities and live weather to stay near the top of the fps range.

KnownIssues: The game requires a very large initial install and ongoing streaming data, which can cause stutters or degraded visuals on slow or metered connections.
Loading times are very long on the Deck's internal SSD; installing to a fast microSD card may worsen this further.
Some UI elements and menus are small and difficult to read on the 7-inch 1280x800 screen.
Online multiplayer and live weather features may cause additional CPU overhead and frame drops.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Removing TDP and GPU limits lets the APU boost fully, which can push the sim close to a sustained 30 fps over open terrain and water; expect drops into the mid-20s over photogrammetry cities regardless of settings. Battery life will be short — keep a charger nearby for long flights.

Optimal.Notes: A 45 Hz refresh with a 30 fps cap provides smooth pacing for flight simulation; medium textures and cloud quality give a noticeably better visual result over low without a dramatic GPU cost. Drop Terrain LOD to 60 if frame rate dips in busy areas.

profiles.Summary: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020 40th Anniversary Edition is a demanding simulation that pushes the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU hard, typically requiring low settings and FSR upscaling to maintain a playable 30 fps. Expect performance to vary significantly by scenario — dense airports and photogrammetry cities will stress the hardware more than open skies.

On your first run, check frame rate during a busy airport departure — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, switch to the Max Battery profile and reduce Terrain LOD further.

The game requires a large installation (~150 GB) and may need significant SSD space management on the Deck.
Online multiplayer and live traffic features may increase CPU load and cause additional frame dips.
VR support is not functional on Steam Deck; ignore VR-related prompts in settings.
